name: Compagnia
key_source:
SCOPE, WRITTEN 2026-08-31 PER LOGBOOK 2 OF THAT DATE: the FLORENTINE term-limited contractual partnership with a subscribed corpo di compagnia and a sopraccorpo of deposits above it. TRADITION NARROWED FROM 'Italian (Latin)' TO 'Tuscan (Florentine)' BY MS ON 2026-08-31; SIENA IS OUT OF SCOPE, for the reason recorded under LR1 below. NOT the generic 'medieval Italian partnership' of the comparative literature, and NOT the Venetian compa(g)nia, which means a short-term joint venture. WHERE A SOURCE USES compagnia GENERICALLY - Hansmann Kraakman & Squire section V throughout, Fleischer & Agstner, Kohn - THE CODER MUST ESTABLISH THAT THE PASSAGE BEARS ON THE TUSCAN CONTRACTUAL FORM BEFORE THE CELL TAKES A VALUE FROM IT, and record that judgement in the cell note. That was done on every HKS-based cell in the 2026-08-31 batch; where it could not be made comfortably - AP1, whose paragraph cites Galgano and Lattes on Italian law generally - the confidence is low and the note says so. ALSO OUT OF SCOPE: the Medici hub-and-spoke holding, in which each branch is a separate partnership with its own constitutive act and its own capital (Sapori 1978, XLIV, XLIV-LXXV; HKS printed 34) - Sapori's own 'dalla compagnia alla holding'. And the societa in accomandita, a distinct form with no row in this census, which from the later fourteenth century supplied the limited liability the compagnia never had (Sapori 1978, XLVI-XLVII).
CODED 2026-08-31 by ai from the vault-blind bundle; unreviewed. 32 cells: 17 substantive, 12 .NR, 3 .NA.
SOURCES ACTUALLY CODED FROM, replacing the previous 'vault: fraterna/compagnia note': Hunt 1994, The Medieval Super-Companies (printed 76-77, 113) from the Peruzzi account books - the row's best source and independent of the legal-historical literature; Sapori 1978, Compagnie e mercanti di Firenze antica (printed XXXVI-XXXVIII, XLIV, XLVI-XLVII, LXXV, XCIII) for unlimited and joint-and-several liability, the corpo, the early contract clauses and the Sienese contrast; English 1988, Enterprise and Liability in Sienese Banking (printed 91-92, 98, 101) for the Sienese material; Hansmann Kraakman & Squire 2006, ECGI Law WP 57/2006 (printed 27-35) for entity shielding, bankruptcy and the household origin.
TWO PROHIBITIONS APPLY TO THIS ROW AND THEY ARE CUMULATIVE. (i) LOGBOOK 2, 2026-08-31: no comparative claim may treat this row and fraterna as two independent cases on any entity-shielding component until they take different values there. (ii) LOGBOOK 1, 2026-08-31: THIS IS A FORM WITH SUB-POOLS - the succursali of the Bardi and Peruzzi (Sapori XXXVII-XXXVIII lists eleven Italian and fourteen foreign branches), each keeping its own books with its own closing date (Hunt 113). The entity locator on LP1, LP2, LP3, AP1, AP2, MG4, FP2 and FP4 is the WHOLE ARRANGEMENT, the recode audit that rule requires has NOT been run, and until it has, no similarity or difference claim on entity-shielding or legal-personality may rest on this row. AP1 is accordingly answered from HKS printed 29-30 and NOT from printed 32, where the shielding is locational and 'each branch of a merchant's business was effectively a distinct entity'; the branch fact has no column and is carried in the AP1 cell note.
CONFIGURATION WORTH A REVIEWER'S ATTENTION: TS1=1 with TS2=fixed-term, against the vocabulary's expectation that 'TS1=1 strongly constrains TS2 toward open'. Hunt printed 76 separates them in terms - the partnerships 'did not dissolve with the death or retirement of a partner' and were 'immediately renewed' on closure, while the contract itself ran one to twelve years. A form whose contract was term-limited and whose business was not.
LR1 IS CODED ON THE FLORENTINE FORM AND SIENA DEPARTS WITHIN THIS ROW'S DECLARED PERIOD AND TRADITION. At the Bonsignori failure the partners obtained from the Nine the right to answer third parties 'non solidalmente', a provision of the costituto of 1310 'non ripetendosi nei costituti posteriori' (Sapori XXXVII); English 91-92 and 98 show the council in 1316-17 allocating Tolomei liability pro rata to capital while holding non-payers jointly liable for the remainder; and the Mercanzia statute of 1342-43 restores the rule - 'Che ciascuno compagno sia tenuto en tutto' (English 101 n.2). Sapori XXXVII draws the contrast the row rests on: at Florence 'si rimase costanti anche per cio che attiene alla struttura giuridica della compagnia, mentre a Siena...'. DECIDED BY MS, 2026-08-31: THE TRADITION FIELD IS TIGHTENED FROM 'Italian (Latin)' TO 'Tuscan (Florentine)' AND SIENA IS PUT OUT OF SCOPE, rather than splitting the row. The alternative considered and rejected was a compagnia_siena row on the standing rule that a type spanning both values of a characteristic must be split (the voc precedent): on present sources it would rest almost entirely on English 1988 and would manufacture agreement on every other cell, which is the begijnhof 1585 situation. FALSIFICATION CONDITION, so this is not a permanent verdict: SPLIT WHEN A SECOND SIENESE SOURCE IS HELD that gives a cell-level value differing from the Florentine one - Senigaglia's edition of the Mercanzia statute (BSSP 14-17, 1907-10), which English cites throughout, is the obvious acquisition. NOTE THE COST OF THE TIGHTENING, WHICH IS REAL: the Sienese evidence at Sapori XXXVII and English 91-92, 98, 101 is now OUT OF SCOPE FOR THE VALUE and is retained in the LR1 cell note as context only. In particular English 1988 - a whole monograph on Sienese liability - drops from being a witness to LR1 to being a witness that the Florentine rule was not universal in Tuscany.
CITATION CAUTION: HKS printed 33-34 report a 1310 Sienese statute restoring pro rata liability and its repeal in 1342, citing English 91-92. English 91-92 is about the Consiglio Generale of November 1316 and January 1317; English 98 mentions statutes of 1312, 1316 and 1319; the 1342-43 Mercanzia statute is at English 101 n.2 and REASSERTS joint liability. HKS's substance survives, their dates and page do not sit together as cited.
WITNESS INDEPENDENCE, THINNER THAN IT LOOKS: HKS printed 29 n.83 cites SAPORI 1955 for the joint-and-several rule, so HKS and Sapori 1978 are one scholar twice on LR1. Hunt 76 and English 101 n.2 are independent of both.
HELD AND NOT READ FOR THIS PASS: Padgett & McLean 2006 and Padgett 2012 on Florentine partnership systems; Kuehn 2008 on Florentine inheritance (the best candidate for a second pass, and the one most likely to bear on the fraterna/compagnia formation contrast); Punta 2018; de Roover 1948 and 1963 (Medici, out of scope). Televantos 2020 is English law c.1780-1830 and supplies analytic vocabulary only.

The old values answered CF2's question. (ii) DONE 2026-08-30: the entity questions LP1-LP3, AP1, AP2, AP4, CI1-CI4 were asked and close three - LP1=0 (Harris 13, 'a nexus of contracts', with sole personal liability toward third parties at 10), AP1=P (Harris 11, the 'asymmetric entity shielding'), CI1=common (van Doosselaere 65, term 1's segregation clause). AP4=.NA on the no-founder disposition shared with bazacle_mill, casa_san_giorgio, the maone and partenrederij, WHICH LEAVES isqa AP4=0 AS THE ONLY SUBSTANTIVE AP4 ON A FORM WITH NO FOUNDER - see the adjudications, which recommend deciding AP4's locator on its own and then recoding all seven forms in one pass. The other six are .NR. PAGE CAUTION: Harris 2007 is an unpaginated conference draft and carries no printed page numbers; citations in this repo are to PDF pages, and the existing 'Harris 2007, 9' at AP3, LR1 and commenda_alloc RB2/RB3 points to PDF 10 in the held file. THE ENTITY FACET DOES NOT SEPARATE THIS ROW FROM societas_maris: the pair takes identical values on all ten, two of them on one shared datum. It separates only on LR6 and CF1, both WP1. PAIRED WITH societas_maris, added 2026-08-18 and coded on the same eleven cells. This row covers the UNILATERAL form; the bilateral form is the other row. CF3=bilateral here means TWO PRINCIPALS and is not the literature's 'bilateral commenda' - see the societas_maris CF3 note.

name: Societas maris (the bilateral commenda; Venetian collegantia)
key_source: ADDED 2026-08-18 as a new type row - the code did not previously exist in this vocabulary, though it does in loss_mitigation_type.csv, where it is now coded. van Doosselaere 2009, 64-68: the Genoese notarial cartularies, 6,764 commenda ties 1154-1315, 93 per cent of all coded maritime ties. p.65 states the two liability rules side by side - the unilateral investor 'bore all liability for loss' and the traveller 'bore no capital risk', while in the bilateral form, 'often called SOCIETAS IN GENOA', 'the liability for loss was proportional to the respective initial investments'. Contribution ratio customarily one third traveller, two thirds investor; profit split equally. Harris 2007, 9-13; Held 2025, 22 for the Ragusan contracts sharing lucrum and damnum in the same proportions. CODED ON EXACTLY THE ELEVEN CHARACTERISTICS commenda CARRIES, so the pair is comparable cell for cell. It separates on two: LR6 (symmetric against upside-only) and CF1 (P against 1). It agrees on AP3, LR1, LR2, LR3, LR4, LR5, CF2, CF3 and TS2. DISSENT, RECORDED NOT RESOLVED: Pryor 1977, Luzzatto 1961, 119 and van Doosselaere 2009, 65 n.7 all hold unilateral and bilateral commenda to be 'essentially the same agreement', the choice turning on the traveller's wealth. Every one of them reaches that on the PAYOUT, where the economics are identical by construction (the arithmetic is at 65 n.6). None reaches it on the loss. The row is kept separate because both of this project's datasets measure the loss. PERIOD NOTE: loss_mitigation_type.csv gives '10-13c' for the same code. That is probably too early for the Genoese evidence, which van Doosselaere's corpus opens in 1154, and the two rows should be reconciled at review. CROSS-DATASET LINK, WHICH cooccurs_with CANNOT EXPRESS: the same code is coded in loss_mitigation_forms (RB1=RB2=shared). check_vocabularies.py normalises the '@dataset' suffix away and then reads societas_maris@loss_mitigation_forms as a self-reference, so the link is recorded here in prose instead. STILL WANTED: Lopez & Raymond 174-184, where the contracts are translated - it would supply the quoted clause van Doosselaere paraphrases. Coded 2026-08-18; see logbook 2 and logbook 4 for that date. VENETIAN EVIDENCE ADDED 2026-08-18 (ii), and it tightens the period. Merelo-Guervos & Molinari 2025 (10.1007/s13278-025-01460-9, open access), on 381 Venetian contracts 1073-1342 from Morozzo della Rocca & Lombardo, Lombardo & Morozzo della Rocca, Bondi Sebellico and Tiepolo, identify the bilateral form AS the societas maris - 'the merchant supplying one-third of capital with equal profit division', which is exactly van Doosselaere's Genoese rule - and report that 'by the early thirteenth century, bilateral contracts had practically disappeared', the Tiepolo Statutes of 1242 regulating only the unilateral type. That matches van Doosselaere's 'the societas disappeared in the thirteenth century' in Genoa. THE EFFECTIVE WINDOW IS THEREFORE c.1073 TO THE EARLY 13c, NOT THROUGH THE 13c, and the '10-13c' on this row is too generous at the late end where it was suspected of being too generous at the early one. The period field on THIS row is set accordingly; loss_mitigation_type.csv still says '10-13c' and the two should be reconciled at review. ENTITY QUESTIONS ASKED 2026-08-30 and coded on the same ten characteristics as commenda, so the pair remains comparable cell for cell. It agrees with commenda on ALL TEN: LP1=0, AP1=P, CI1=common, AP4=.NA, and .NR on LP2, LP3, AP2, CI2, CI3, CI4. LP1 and AP1 are ONE DATUM SHARED WITH commenda, not two witnesses - Harris 11 describes the family and introduces the bilateral variant only at 12, where the sole stated effect is on profit-splitting - and both carry low confidence here against medium there, on the same reasoning as the 2026-08-18 AP3 and LR1 cells. CI1 is the one cell coded from a sentence naming THIS form: van Doosselaere 65, term 1, 'To the capital received, the traveler might also add his own capital ... in this case, the agreement was called a bilateral commenda' - one merged venture stock. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DISSENT RECORDED ABOVE: Pryor, Luzzatto and van Doosselaere 65 n.7 hold the two forms 'essentially the same agreement' on the PAYOUT, and this row was kept separate because both datasets measure the LOSS. The entity pass is the first evidence on the third question, entity STRUCTURE, and it finds no difference. NO COMPARATIVE CLAIM MAY TREAT THE PAIR AS TWO INDEPENDENT CASES ON ANY WP2 COMPONENT.

name: Mudaraba
key_source: NOT CODED HERE, AND THIS IS A DETERMINATION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION - the same disposition as ortoq_alloc in loss_mitigation_type.csv. Mudarabah is the HANAFI name for the institution coded in this dataset as 'qirad'. Ramli 2018, 97 on al-Sarakhsi's Kitab al-Mudarabah: al-Sarakhsi treats muqaradah as synonymous with mudarabah, 'the Malikites, Shafi'ites and Hanbalites unanimously use a different term i.e. qirad to denote such an activity', and 'in general, be it mudarabah, or muqaradah or qirad, it is by definition a commercial association whereby an investor or capital provider (rabb al-mal) entrusts some amount of capital to an agent... who trades with it and shares with the investor a pre-determined proportion of the profits'. Coding both rows would enter one institution twice and manufacture agreement between them on every cell. FALSIFICATION CONDITION, so this is not a permanent verdict. The schools are not known to diverge on any of the 32 characteristics, but one candidate is live and unverified: the vault note [[The mudaraba is revocable not locked in]] records that classical fiqh predominantly classifies the contract as an 'aqd ja'iz (revocable) while 'Maliki jurists restrict revocation once the agent has commenced work', flagged there as needing verification against fiqh sources. If that holds, mudarabah (Hanafi) and qirad (Maliki) separate on TS3 revocability - a WP2 capital-lock-in question, not a trivial one - and mudaraba earns a row. Note that qirad's own TS3 is currently uncoded, so the test cannot be run from what is in the matrix; it needs a Maliki source, which the library does not hold. Coded 2026-08-18; see logbook 2 and logbook 4 for that date.

name: Fraterna
key_source:
SCOPE, WRITTEN 2026-08-31 PER LOGBOOK 2 OF THAT DATE, BECAUSE THE SOURCES USE THE WORDS LOOSELY AND THE ROW MUST FIX ITS OWN REFERENT: the Venetian undivided fraternal patrimony - co-heir brothers declining to partition the paternal estate, which continues as a trading unit. Membership is co-heirship. NOT any Italian family partnership generally, and NOT the Venetian compa(g)nia, which in Venetian usage means a short-term joint venture (Ryabova 2019, 231) and is a different thing again from the Tuscan compagnia of the other row.
CODED 2026-08-31 by ai from the vault-blind bundle; unreviewed. 32 cells: 14 substantive, 16 .NR, 2 .NA.
SOURCES ACTUALLY CODED FROM, replacing the previous 'vault: fraterna/compagnia note' (the note is withheld and was not read): Lane 1944 (JEH 4:2, 10.1017/S0022050700081304, printed 178-196, READ IN FULL) for formation, capital and the household character; Ryabova 2019 (10.36253/978-88-6453-857-0.13, printed 229-253) for the definition, equal shares, equal administrative powers and the division procedure; Ryabova 2018 (10.2308/AAHJ-10580) for the Soranzo capital account; Gonzalez de Lara 2011 (10.1057/9780230116665_5, printed 108-109) for formation without formal contracts and for the Venetian rule on a father's debts; Morche 2020 (10.11588/heidok.00027656, NO MEASURED PAGE OFFSET - cited by PDF page) for common ownership of the inheritance and the exclusion of female heirs.
THE ROW IS THIN AT THE BARRIER AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT THE LITERATURE, NOT A CODING FAILURE. AP1, AP3, LR1, LP1, LP2, LP3, CI3 and CI4 are all .NR. Lane's nineteen pages use 'fraterna' on eight, 'liabilit*' on two, and 'unlimited' on none; Ryabova 2018 and 2019 together use 'creditor' three times and 'third part*' never. Nothing held asks whether fraterna creditors were prior to a brother's personal creditors, or whether a brother's estate answered to the fraterna's creditors.
PROHIBITION CARRIED FROM LOGBOOK 2, 2026-08-31: this row and compagnia may not be treated as two independent cases on any entity-shielding component until they take different values there. They currently take the same value on exactly one, AP2=0, and that agreement was PREDICTED by the withheld vault note before any evidence was gathered - it is recorded and must not be used. The two 0s also rest on unrelated mechanisms (a co-heir's right to demand division here; cross-infection of bankruptcy there), so they are not two witnesses to one fact.
ONE DATUM, THREE CELLS: AP2=0, CI2=0 and TS3=1 all rest on the division procedure. The capital-immobility group is collinear on this row by construction.
PERIOD FLAGGED AND NOT CHANGED, as logbook 2 left it. The row reads 12-15c. Gonzalez de Lara printed 109 has the fraterna 'of little importance until the mid thirteenth century'; against that, LANE'S ARTICLE - the row's principal source - IS LARGELY SIXTEENTH-CENTURY, its Pisani case running to the brothers' deaths c.1528, and Ryabova's Soranzo material is 1406-1434. THE CODED CELLS THEREFORE REST ON EVIDENCE THAT STRADDLES AND OVERRUNS THE STATED PERIOD AT THE LATE END. Press both against Lane 1944b, Andrea Barbarigo, Merchant of Venice, before amending.
WANTED, AND THE ROW WOULD CHANGE IF THEY ARRIVE: Lane 1944b Andrea Barbarigo (cited by Ryabova 2018 at printed 202-205 for this very fraterna and NOT in the library); Pertile, Storia del diritto italiano III, 274-284, which both Lane and Morche name as the standard legal account; Fumagalli, Il diritto di fraterna (1912). Any of them may close LR1 and AP1.

name: Ortoq — equity regime (capital entrusted)
key_source: Enkhbold 2019 (Central Asian Survey 38:4, 10.1080/02634937.2019.1652799), 542-543, from Juvayni, Rashid al-Din and Vassaf. SPLIT from the generic 'ortoq' row: the type spans both values of AP3, CF2, LR1 and LR6, which one row cannot hold. Principal bears losses capped at his investment, agent bears none — the qirad/commenda configuration. NOT A PHASE: Enkhbold has loan financing adopted 'when Ogedei and Mongke ruled', i.e. contemporaneous with the equity examples from Ogedei's own reign, so equity and loan are COEXISTING CONTRACT TYPES whose relative prevalence shifted, not a sequence. Dates deliberately left unperiodised. NOT AN INDEPENDENT OBSERVATION from ortoq_loan — one institution, two contract forms; organizational_form_type.csv has no cooccurs_with column in which to say so.

name: Ortoq — loan regime (capital advanced at interest)
key_source: Enkhbold 2019, 543-544, on Allsen 1989 and Otagi 1973. The second half of the split: ortoqs 'completely liable for the loans they took, which extended beyond partnership capital to their private properties'; guarantors unconditionally bound; on default, seizure and then enslavement of the defaulter and his family (Rashid al-Din 1998, 726). The isqa configuration. Attested from Ogedei's and Mongke's reigns and 'eventually became prevalent... by the end of the thirteenth century'. Enkhbold's stated cause for the shift in prevalence: the government spent 76,000 ding of silver in 1240 bailing out ortoqs, and 'the huge losses suffered by Mongol elites motivated Mongol authorities to shift towards a risk-transfer model'. NOT AN INDEPENDENT OBSERVATION from ortoq_equity.

name: Maona di Chio (New Maona)

name: Partenrederij / Partenreederei (fractional ship co-ownership)
tradition: Low Countries (Holland); the term reder migrated into German
period: 15c onward; coded on Hollandic law c.1619-1625
key_source: De ruysscher 2023 (Grotiana 44:2, 10.1163/18760759-44020002, open access), 334-365, and specifically 336-343 for the liability rules and 357-358 for the form itself: 'Ship co-owning associations had grown out of the co-ownership of ships. Such partenrederij had been used at least since the beginning of the fifteenth century. It was a fractional joint ownership, which allowed for pooling investments in costly ships.' CODED FROM ONE SOURCE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING ABOUT THE SOURCE BASE RATHER THAN A SHORTCUT. Of the five ship items in the Zotero collection 'HistorEE - beguinage and fractional ship ownership', only this one treats the Low Countries / German form: Haff 1910 is about medieval LAND and river transport cooperatives (Rott, Rottfuhren, carters' and boatmen's guilds - 121 occurrences of 'Rott' against 11 of 'Schiff', none of them about part-ownership) and contains no partenrederij material; Ebel 1975 is a two-page review of Ruhwedel, Die Partenreederei, with no attachment held and the book itself not in the library; Scammell 1962 and Steckley 2020 are ENGLISH part-ownership and are a different tradition - see the proposed-of adjudications, which recommend a separate type rather than folding them in. SCOPE: this row is the partenrederij STRICTLY - fractional co-ownership of the ship. De ruysscher 358 distinguishes it from the OPEN REDERIJ, in which 'the participants... were simple investors in a stock that was not the ship itself', and records that Grotius blended the two. Folding the open rederij in would make CI1 and CF1 span both values and require a split under the rule applied to voc on 2026-08-29. PERIOD AND EVIDENCE ARE NOT CO-EXTENSIVE, WHICH IS THE ROW'S MAIN WEAKNESS: the institution is attested from the early fifteenth century, but every coded liability cell rests on Grotius's Inleidinge (1619/1631) and De iure belli ac pacis (1625), and De ruysscher's own argument is that a general right of abandonment 'did not exist before Grotius put it to text' (350-351) and that Grotius 'stood on the sideline' of the development (363). AP3 and LR1 therefore carry low confidence. DESCENT CLAIM RECORDED, NOT ADOPTED: Gelderblom and Jonker (2004, 2010) make partenrederij a precursor of the voorcompagnieen and ultimately the VOC on continuity of fractional ownership and limited liability (356-357); Punt and de Jongh reject it, on the grounds that voorcompagnie participants had no right of abandonment and that voorcompagnie capital 'was not split up in portions, as was the case in the rederij' (357). The cooccurs_with link to the voc rows carries basis 'uncertain' for that reason. Note the repo's reserved terminology: any relation here would be PARALLELISM or descent, never 'convergence', since a shared ancestral condition is exactly what is in dispute. VAULT: no note on this form existed before this batch; the adjacent notes are on bodemerij, and [[The Bodmerei shield was a default rule and Amsterdam contracted out of it]] bears directly on AP3 and LR1 because its Amsterdam protests execute against the reders' persons and whole estates. Coded 2026-08-29 by ai; unreviewed.

name: Begijnhof / court beguinage (curtis beguinarum)
tradition: Low Countries (Southern Netherlands; also Lille, Valenciennes, Breda, Amsterdam)
key_source: Moran 2018 (Journal of Early Modern History 22:1-2, 10.1163/15700658-17-00010), 67-95, read in full - the single indispensable source, and unusually well matched to this matrix because its subject IS governance and financial administration. Its key structural statement, at 77: 'The Court Beguinages were internally divided into a standardized set of sub-institutions, each of which was financially independent from the others; these were the hof or court, the infirmary, the church, and the Table of the Holy Ghost... each sub-institution was legally a separate body and none could be held responsible for the others' debts.' Supported by Overlaet 2015 (in Single Life and the City, 1200-1900, 10.1057/9781137406408_7), 138-157, on the Great Beguinage of St Catherine in Mechelen from 40 beguine wills of 1532-91, and by Voigt 2012 (in Friedensnobelpreis und historische Grundlagenforschung, 10.1515/9783110259551.441), 441-476, on the legal status of the beguine way of life after the Council of Vienne in the dioceses of Cambrai, Tournai, Liege and Utrecht. SCOPE: THE COURT BEGUINAGE (begijnhof, curtis) ONLY. Moran 68 n.2 draws the line this row observes: the term was 'used to distinguish these large and consistently structured communities from smaller, less stable groups (begijngemeenschappen or begijnkonventen)', and 'whereas the Court Beguinages were incredibly stable ... the smaller beguine communities were far more transient'. Deregnaucourt 2000 in the same Zotero collection is about the hopital des Wetz at Douai - a couvent of about 27 beguines with an average stay of four years ten months - which is that contrast class, and is not coded here. It is in any case unreadable: its PERSEE PDF carries a text layer on the two cover pages only, the eighteen body pages extracting empty. PERIOD AND EVIDENCE ARE UNEVENLY MATCHED, AND THE ROW SHOULD PROBABLY BE SPLIT. Almost every entity-level coding here - LP1, LP2, LP3, CI1, TS4, MG2 - rests on Moran and is therefore post-1585. Three cells give positive evidence that the medieval position differed: TS4 (Moran 80 presents episcopal statute-making as a change that decreased the beguinages' autonomy), MG4 (Voigt 443, 475: a way of life following no supra-regionally binding rule, under no superior instance, 'nicht approbiert' yet held in high standing, its communities seeking Schutzprivilegien from secular rulers), and LP1 (Voigt 470: an Osnabrueck property transaction of 1320 requiring the consent of all 37 named beguines, in a community with no fixed enclosure and no hierarchy - though that community is a Domschwesternhaus and so the contrast class). A split at 1585 on the voc_1602/voc_1612/voc_1623 model is the obvious remedy and is NOT proposed in this batch, because on present sources both halves would rest on Moran and the split would manufacture agreement rather than test it. See the proposed-of adjudications. THE FORM'S CONTRIBUTION: LP3=1 is the first 1 on that characteristic in the matrix, and LR4=1 with LR5=diversifying is the third 1 and second 'diversifying' on the risk-pooling facet. Coded 2026-08-29 by ai; unreviewed. FALSIFICATION CONDITION FOR THE SPLIT, SO THE ONE-ROW DECISION IS NOT A PERMANENT VERDICT. The split at 1585 was considered and REJECTED for this batch, on the reasoning in the proposed-of adjudications: of the three cells that looked like medieval/early-modern divergence, LP1's counter-case (Voigt 470) is a Domschwesternhaus and therefore Moran's contrast class rather than evidence about the court form; MG4 would come out .NR on BOTH rows, since the dual secular-and-ecclesiastical subjection Moran reports at 79 as having 'always' obtained is matched in Voigt's medieval material by episcopal commissions under Cum de mulieribus alongside Schutzprivilegien from secular rulers; and TS4's medieval value is not established either, because Voigt 443 says no superior instance was competent in matters of law and form of life, which asserts that NOBODY could amend the rules rather than that the entity could. A split on present sources would also put 21 of 22 substantive cells on one side and leave the other nearly empty, which is the mudaraba situation - two rows resting on one source manufacture agreement rather than test it. THE STANDING CAUTION, WHICH IS THE REAL REASON FOR WAITING: 1585 is where the SOURCE BASE begins, not demonstrably where the institution moved. Moran's article opens in the 1580s because her archives do. Splitting there would encode a periodisation drawn from record survival into the matrix, where a later reader would take the difference between the two rows for a finding about beguinages. That 1585 is also a genuine watershed in the world - Revolt, Trent, the 1559 episcopal reorganisation taking effect, the bishops taking the right to appoint the beguinage priests - is not by itself a reason to split; the test is whether a CHARACTERISTIC moved. SPLIT THIS ROW WHEN a medieval source gives a cell-level value that differs from Moran's on any of: TS4 (who held the power to amend the statutes before the bishops claimed it after 1585); LP1 or LP2 (whether a medieval court beguinage held property as an entity - the Ghent foundation charters Moran mentions at 80 n.24, which gave the grand mistresses and momboren the right to appoint the priests, are the lead); or MG2 (whether the grand mistress was elected before 1585). Philippen, De Begijnhoven: Oorsprong, geschiedenis, inrichting (Antwerp 1918) is the acquisition that would settle it - Moran 68 n.2 calls it the foundational overview of the Court Beguinages and their institutional structures and cites it for election procedures and for the text of the 1588 Mechelen statutes - with Simons, Cities of Ladies (2001) alongside.

name: Avarız akçesi vakfı (mahalle/köy extraordinary-levy endowment)
key_source: NEW ROW, 2026-09-04, coded from four Turkish-language sources read in full. SCOPE, AND IT HAD TO BE FIXED BEFORE A CELL COULD BE OPENED: the endowment (akar or para vakfı) constituted for ONE FISCAL COMMUNITY UNIT to meet its share of the avârız, nüzul and kürekçi bedeli and, once the levy lost its importance, the unit's collective needs. NOT the avârız hâne, which is the accounting unit by which the levy was apportioned, and NOT the avârız itself: that error of fact was caught and corrected on the loss-census row avariz_fund on 2026-08-19 and is not repeated here. THE UNIT IS THE FISCAL COMMUNITY, NOT AUTOMATICALLY THE MAHALLE, and the reason is in the evidence. Kırkçeşme in Kastamonu is one mahalle with one 6,280-kuruş corpus (Küçük 2025, 154). Ammu mahalle in Ayntab is divided into NINE bölük/hâne, each with its own mütevelli and its own separate cash summing to 857.5 kuruş, and Alineccar into two (Kıvrım 2019, 39, Tablo 1). Scoped to the mahalle the row would span both values of CI1 and would be a SUB-POOL FORM within the meaning of logbook 1, 2026-08-31, whose standing prohibition would then bar any entity-shielding or legal-personality claim resting on it until the sub-pool audit is run. Scoped to the fiscal unit the locator rule returns each fund as a whole arrangement by its own final clause. A REVIEWER WHO PREFERS THE MAHALLE SCOPING MUST APPLY THAT PROHIBITION TO THIS ROW. SOURCES. Küçük 2025, Osmanlı Medeniyeti Araştırmaları Dergisi 24, 147-183, 10.21021/osmed.1472954 - the Kırkçeşme avarız akçesi vakıf defteri, 1249/1834-1284/1867, the fullest accounting source. Kars 2020, Tarih Araştırmaları Dergisi 40/69, 160-187, 10.35239/tariharastirmalari.780977 - İstanbul şer'iyye sicilleri nrs 3, 10, 12, 18, 20, 22, 1618-1697, 36 funds tabulated with founder, trustee and sum. Kıvrım 2019, Gaziantep Üniversitesi Ayntab Araştırmaları Dergisi 2/2, 34-49 - 17c Ayntab, nine mahalle funds accounted at court in 1692. Gürsoy 2019, on the Evkaf Muhasebeciliği court 1491-1828, 109 waqfs of which 38 avarız. All four read in full 2026-09-04; page offsets taken from the Zotero Extra fields and not re-derived. CITATION FLAG, NOT REPAIRED: Zotero dates Kars 2020 while the article's own running head reads TAD C.40/S.69, 2021, 160-187. The loss census cites 'Kars 2020' and this row follows it for consistency; one of the two is wrong and it should be settled before print. THREE INDEPENDENCE PROBLEMS, DECLARED BEFORE THE ROW WAS WRITTEN AND NOT AFTER. (i) THE SHARPEST ONE. Küçük 2025 is the source behind avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme's accounting cells in loss_mitigation_forms AND is this row's best entity source. Wherever a cell here and a cell there rest on the same page of the same author the two censuses are not independent evidence and no agreement between them is a finding. The pages at risk are Küçük 147-156 and 161, which carry avariz_vakfi_kirkcesme's MC1, LS1, PY0-PY2, VF1, DR1, RB3 and PR1 and this row's LR3, LR4, CI2, TS1, LR2 and FP4. (ii) KARS 2020 AND KIVRIM 2019 ARE ONE WITNESS ON THE NORMS AND TWO ON THE CASES. Kıvrım was accepted 31-12-2019 and Kars 03-10-2020; Kars carries Kıvrım in his bibliography and cites him. The sentence on trustees being elected by the residents and registered at court, and the sentence on the waqf's claim carrying no privilege, appear in both with the city swapped, and the second descends from Akgündüz. What is genuinely separate is Kıvrım's Ayntab court evidence (Kanalıcı, Kayser, the 1706 vekil election) and Kars's Istanbul replacement evidence. This was recorded in the loss census on 2026-08-19 (iv) and was confirmed here by reading both. (iii) THIS ROW SHARES A DOCTRINAL SUBSTRATE WITH waqf_khayri, and the census has no way to say so. Agreement at TS1, TS2, CI2, LR2, LR4, MG1 and FP1 rests on the law of vakıf, not on two observations of two institutions. cooccurrence_basis names institutional relations only; the value this needs would be something like 'same-legal-genus', and logbook 5 (2026-08-19) already asked for a neighbouring value ('same-analytic-frame') and did not get one. FLAGGED, NOT REPAIRED. WHAT THE ROW SEPARATES ON, AND IT IS THE RESULT. MG2=collective against waqf_khayri's founder-fixed, on Kıvrım's own Ayntab appointment cases and Kars's Istanbul replacements. LP2=1 against waqf_khayri's P, and LP3=1 where waqf_khayri is P. TS3=P against waqf_khayri's 0, on Gürsoy's rücû evidence. Four substantive separations from the census's other waqf, all from register and court evidence rather than from doctrine. NO boundary_basis / boundary_confidence COLUMNS EXIST IN THIS VOCABULARY, so the reasoning above has nowhere structured to live. Same gap recorded at logbook 2, 2026-08-29. On the loss side this row would carry boundary_basis=structural-difference at high.

name: Confraternity / lay religious confraternity (umbrella)
key_source: UMBRELLA ROW, NOT CODED, CREATED 2026-09-04 TO CARRY A SCOPE DECISION RATHER THAN A CODING. The commission was to code 'confraternita - the lay religious confraternity of Latin Christendom, treated as an organizational form'. IT IS NOT CODED AS ONE ROW, and the reasons are the sources' own. (1) THE TWO HELD TRADITIONS ARE NOT ONE FORM ON THE POINTS THIS DATASET ASKS ABOUT. Klieber 2001 (Salzburg 1600-1950) contrasts his post-Tridentine Bruderschaft with 'vielen mittelalterlichen Vorgängern' precisely on free access (printed 47-48), with the Venetian scuole grandi and other Italian confraternite on political role (printed 61), and with the romance lands on the charitable dimension, which he finds 'ein eher bescheidenes und eindeutig nachrangiges Engagement' in Salzburg and better preserved in the south (printed 57-59). Gazzini 2020 restricts herself to Italian religious associations 'only when they were mainly composed of professionals' (printed 173) and treats corporazioni and confraternite as contiguous and in some periods indistinguishable (printed 171). A single row would take its values from two authors who each say their object differs from the other's, and any divergence inside it would be an artefact of tradition rather than of institution. (2) LOGBOOK 2 ALREADY CARRIED THE INSTRUCTION. The standing note of 2026-08-13, taken from this very Klieber article, says the loss-census confraternity_fund 'cannot be one row for Latin Christendom'. It was honoured there by splitting; it is honoured here by not creating a single row in the first place. (3) ONLY ONE OF THE TWO CAN CARRY AN organizational_forms ROW. Gazzini's chapter and its Italian twin are about mutual support and crypto-insurance; they answer almost nothing about legal personality, asset partitioning, capital lock-in, transferable claims or succession, and they are already the source of confraternity_fund_it in the loss census, so coding from them here would enter one witness twice. Klieber answers property, capital, governance, membership, entry, authorisation, succession and purpose. THE CODED CHILD IS THEREFORE bruderschaft_salzburg AND NOT AN ITALIAN ROW. WHAT THIS ROW IS FOR: to hold the split, on the confraternity_fund and guild_mutual_aid model, so that an Italian child can be cut when a source is acquired that puts the entity questions to the confraternita. THE ACQUISITION THAT WOULD DO IT is Frank, 'Bruderschaften als Bank. Italienische Beispiele des 15. und 16. Jahrhunderts' (Zotero UNWASN6P), which has NO ATTACHMENT and is the item that would have carried the capital questions; and behind it the confraternity-as-universitas literature, which no held item treats. NOT CODED, DELIBERATELY: every one of the 32 characteristics. This is a determination, not an omission.

name: Bruderschaft / Liebesbund (post-Tridentine Salzburg 'Fraternität')
key_source: NEW ROW, 2026-09-04. THE CODED CHILD OF confraternita, narrowed to what the one source that answers entity questions actually covers: the post-Tridentine Bruderschaft and Liebesbund of the city and archdiocese of Salzburg, 1600-1950, in Klieber's own term of art the 'Fraternität'. SCOPE, IN KLIEBER'S DEFINITION (printed 50): organisations in the form of voluntary, freely accessible, precept-rich but legally and morally non-binding associations of persons for the building of spiritual funds for a well-prepared, worthy and pain-reduced passage from life to eternal blessedness, requiring for official status the approbation of the competent ecclesiastical authority with effect on title, indulgences, statutes and supervision. His typology has three axes - geziert/zierlos, selbständig/betreut, einfach/affiliiert - and the row spans all three. NOT the Marian congregations, which Klieber excludes from the category on free access and bindingness, and NOT the nineteenth-century catholic Vereine that borrowed the name. SOURCE. Klieber 2001, Revue d'Histoire Ecclésiastique 96/1-2, 34-70, 10.1484/J.RHE.3.2, read in full 2026-09-04; printed = PDF + 33 per the Zotero Extra, not re-derived. It reports a 1998 Habilitationsschrift built on serial sources - Einschreibbücher and Jahresrechnungen of about forty city associations plus a survey of the Land - so the quantities are the study's, not the article's. ONE SOURCE, AND THE ROW'S THIRTEEN .NR CELLS ARE MOSTLY THAT FACT: Klieber's field is the organisation type, its Totendienst, its membership and its finances, and he never puts the questions of personhood, standing, creditor priority or liability. His own term sweep confirms it - no Rechtsperson, no juristische Person, no Körperschaft anywhere in 37 pages. CO-OCCURRENCE, AND A DEPARTURE FROM THE COMMISSION THAT MUST BE VISIBLE. The brief directed that cooccurrence_basis=same-institution be set against the loss-census row confraternity_fund_it. UNDER THIS SCOPE DECISION THAT DECLARATION WOULD BE FALSE: confraternity_fund_it is Gazzini's medieval Italian material and this row is Klieber's early-modern Salzburg material - different institution, region and centuries. The relation that does hold is to the confraternita umbrella above, and it is declared. THE RELATION TO confraternity_fund_it IS EVIDENTIAL AND NOT INSTITUTIONAL - both reach the census through one analyst's question set, the guild-and-confraternity mutual-support frame of the Hellwege volume - and cooccurrence_basis has no value for that. Logbook 5, 2026-08-19 asked for one ('same-analytic-frame') and did not get it. FLAGGED, NOT REPAIRED. NOTE ALSO that Klieber's Salzburg material is the row the loss census DELIBERATELY PARKED on 2026-08-19: 'The Salzburg row stays parked... worth cutting precisely BECAUSE it is close to a null.' It is cut here on the entity side and remains uncut on the loss side, so the two censuses do not double-count it. THE ROW'S OPEN QUESTION, AND IT IS MG2. Klieber's second typological axis divides selbständige fraternities, which had their own Präfekt, Assistenten, Konsilium and lay Verwalter and ran their own finances, from betreute ones whose leadership and financial competence lay with the abbot, superior, rector or reverend mother of the religious community - and the largest body in the study, the Skapulierbruderschaft of St. Peter, is of the second kind. The type therefore spans two values of MG2 and the standing rule says split. SPLITTING IS NOT PROPOSED, because two rows would rest on this one source and would manufacture agreement on every other cell - the mudaraba and begijnhof-1585 situation. FALSIFICATION CONDITION: split selbständig from betreut when a second Salzburg or south-German source gives a cell-level value that differs across the two. Katzinger on the Upper Austrian towns and Ardaillou on Vienna, both cited by Klieber, are the obvious candidates. NO boundary_basis / boundary_confidence COLUMNS EXIST HERE. On the loss side this row would carry boundary_basis=documented-instance at high: it exists because one dated, localised body of serial evidence was read, not because it was shown to differ structurally from an Italian confraternity, which could not be assessed.
